notes: Extracted unchanged except the four anonymous rules are named rule:tx-*. odrl:conflict is absent as in DPROD, so the profile default (odrl:prohibit) applies. Two recurring duties with different bearers: rule:tx-delivery names the finance team (the grantor, so DPROD would put it in grantorDuties were it ever collected); rule:tx-report names no subjectOfDuty, so after policy-level interiorisation (assigner only) its bearer is the request subject (due2-profiles.md §6) — the consumer's reporting duty, in DPROD's shape but collected by neither party set (the no-subject gap, due2-profiles.md §8.2). Monthly recurrence from anchor 2026-05-01 (delivery, BYMONTHDAY=1) and 2026-05-15 (report, BYMONTHDAY=15): occurrences on the same day-of-month as the anchor, at the anchor's time. DPROD's expand is clock-anchored with no DTSTART and performed has no lower bound (§8.2); where activation is supplied, dprod_expected assumes the same occurrences and Σ from the same evidence (exception 2). DPROD duty collection (§7.2 step 1): deliver and report never match read. Intended §7.4 reading throughout.

scenarios.name: June read: last month's cycle missed, this month's open

expected.why: rule:tx-read is ready and the export prohibition does not match read: Permit. Both obligations are in force. From anchor 2026-05-01, BYMONTHDAY=1 yields 05-01 and 06-01 by effective_at, each with a three-day deadline: the first is past with no witness (violated), the second's window runs to 06-04 (outstanding). From anchor 2026-05-15, BYMONTHDAY=15 yields 05-15 by effective_at, deadline 05-20 passed, no witness: violated; the 06-15 occurrence is not yet owed. The two violations are reported and cost nothing (§6.1).

scenarios.dprod_expected: Permit (neither deliver nor report matches read, so no duty is collected; the permission is active)

expected.why: rule:tx-no-export matches ex:export by equality; the read permission does not match (export is not below read). Deny. No obligation is in force: no permission or prohibition of the policy matches an export, which is what in force turns on.

Nothing matches modify: it is not below read or export (all three sit under use as siblings), and modify is below no rule here. The policy governs reads and exports of this asset, not modifications: NotApplicable.
